message.content:
The total number of distinct positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large – on the order of **10⁴³**.  

This figure, often referred to as the *Shannon number*, is an estimate of the number of legal positions reachable from the starting position under normal rules. It gives you a sense of how vast the combinatorial space of chess really is.
